title: Jam sessions at her house with Lloyd Wilson
summary: Lloyd Wilson brought visiting musicians to her home near Central Avenue, where Eddie Barefield, Panama Francis and Benny Carter jammed.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: was a little premature baby, so -- and we used to -- we lived not far from -- still in that same neighborhood. It was so wonderful that I managed to live and stay in that same neighborhood all this time, until 1947, you know, when I started recording. Then I moved to the west side. But all this time I lived right up in that area. And the guys used to come to my house. My husband and I had a little house and we shared this house with another musician, Lloyd Wilson, and his wife. He was a trumpet player. He worked here. He used to work at a place called Papke's. That's another place that comes to mind. It was a very popular place. It wasn't -- I don't think it was a plush place.
Papke's was a dance place, somewhere downtown.
I've never heard of it before.

Papke's. It was called Papke's. And this guy, anyway, he got to know a lot of musicians, Lloyd did, Lloyd Wilson, he got to know an awful lot of musicians. He did know a lot of musicians because he was from Texas, but he had lived back east quite awhile, and particularly in Detroit. He lived in Detroit. So he used to meet the musicians when they'd come to town, you know, and they'd bring them to our house, you know. And they'd come to our house, he'd bring them over and he wasn't what you'd call a great trumpet player, by far he

was not. But he was a nice guy, very personable, and all the guys just loved Lloyd Wilson, and he used to bring these guys to the house, and we would jam. That's what we used to do, have jam sessions at my house, you know. And I got the chance to meet so many marvelous musicians at that particular time. Eddie Barefield was one guy that I met. I met Panama Francis in those years, years ago. I met -- I met -- well, I think Benny, I think I met Benny Carter, if I'm thinking correctly, at that time. Anyway, they all used to just --
Well, I've heard. In interviewing musicians that we all used to go over to Nellie's place and jam.
As soon as you came into town you always went over to see Nellie.
